what_this_is: How rulings on single lines are kept, read by do-work/ruling-records.mjs and do-work/rulings.mjs: each is a row of the person's generic Checks list (list:checks), a record `record_type` with id `id_prefix`<hex of the BLAKE3 of [text, verdict, by, rule]>, of kind `kinds.ruled` (a good or bad ruling, a labelled line like the decider's) or `kinds.escalated` (a line a checker escalated, no verdict on it yet), part_of the rule it was given under, or the branch the caller names when it names no rule. The ruling's own copy kind is kept as `line_kind`, so it never collides with the row's kind. Then the words of every refusal.

words.refused_rows: rows and existing are lists of rulings; refuse is a list of { field, one_of?: [values], contains_one_of?: [path parts] }; hand_rulings is { field: [words] }; place is { field, pattern }; escalated_verdicts is a list of words.
words.refused_row: Every ruling needs its text (the line), verdict (one word, such as bad, good or escalated) and by (who gave it).
words.refused_parent: A ruling that names no rule is kept under the branch unruled_part_of names (the person's setting, such as content-production); give it.
words.refused_fixture: REFUSED: {count} row(s) come from a test piece or a temporary folder (the list's refuse setting); they never go into the person's rulings. Nothing is written.
words.refused_word: A ruling given by hand needs its {field} to be one of {words}; it is {value}.
